text:
sasha: heads up — seeing a weird regression when bringing up the awq-quantized build of the new llama2-13b fp8->awq pipeline. some tool-call responses have missing args keys, JSON still parses but required fields are gone.

maria: can you paste a tiny repro and confirm whether gptq/generic int8 also shows this?

sasha: quick repro (local dedicated canary):
```bash
# run simple chat that triggers tool call
redwood-cli infer --model rdx/llama2-13b-fp8-awq --stream true --prompt-file failing_prompt.txt
```
example output (notice missing params):
```json
{"role":"tool","name":"weather","args":{}}
# expected: {"location":"sf","units":"metric"} inside args or a params key
```

lee: interesting — is kvcache/streaming on? that combo has bitten us before.

sasha: yes kvcache enabled and streaming true. if i disable streaming or clear kvcache between calls the problem disappears.

tom: sounds like a partial emit from the runtime when kv cache prefix is reused + awq token boundary. might be tokenization/cutoff mid-object. can you share a server log snippet around the emit?

sasha: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T14:22:30Z INFO emit_chunk id=abc123 tokens=78 partial=true
2026-03-18T14:22:30Z WARN structured_emit truncated_object key_start=23 key_end=56
2026-03-18T14:22:30Z DEBUG kvcache reuse hit=true prefix_len=512
```

deploy-bot: canary deploy awq-runtime v1.4.3 -> v1.4.4 scheduled to 10% hosts (manual rollback enabled) :rocket:

maria: can you bisect awq runtime? which awq commit introduced quant conversion flags? also does gptq show same?

sasha: gptq/int8 builds are clean on this prompt. looks specific to awq-quant path. model id: rdx/llama2-13b-fp8 -> converted with awq v1.4.3 using `--perchannel --blocksize 128 --symmetry=dynamic`. only reproducible when temperature >= 0.7 and stream=true. conversion command: 
```bash
awq-convert --input ./fp8/llama2-13b --out ./awq/llama2-13b-awq --per-channel --bs 128
```

lee: ok i can run a narrow bisect across awq commits and the runtime changes. i'll run batch=1 streaming toggles and kvcache on/off.

tom: short-term workaround: force stream buffer to emit whole-object boundaries — e.g., post-process emitter to aggregate until closing brace before handing to JSON parser, or disable kvcache for toolcall routes. also add failing prompt to regression suite so canary fails fast.

sasha: doing that now — i'll add failing prompt + paired test that toggles kvcache/streaming and pin the canary to block if outputs drop required keys. thanks y'all, will post results from the bisect. :thumbsup:
